This action was corrected with education provided as to why the barrier is an important step in the hand washing process. Ensure proper training is accomplished for all employees on how to properly wash hands from start to finish.
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Many areas in the facility are in need of a general cleaning. These areas include, but are not limited to, shelving, counters, and tabletops in the facility. Ensure these areas are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency that prevents the accumulation of soil residue and debris.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The facility is in need of a general and deep cleaning of floors and other various hard to reach surfaces behind equipment. Ensure cleaning takes place at a frequency to prevent soil and debris accumulation.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The fridge under the sliding door cooler by the single service items was observed to leak water. This water is being caught by two pans under the doors. Ensure this equipment is repaired or discarded to prevent the water leaking.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The hand sink by the single service items is in need of caulking where the metal meets the wall. Ensure this area is sealed to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface where debris and other residues are unable to accumulate.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: 2-301.14: Employee was observed to exit the facility and reenter and immediately resume their assigned duties without washing their hands. This behavior was ceased immediately by the inspector and employee was requested to wash their hands. Inspector spoke with PIC to ensure reminders and proper training are reinforced with the staff.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: The baffle, the plastic piece in the ice machine, was observed to be visibly soiled with what appears to be mold growth or another foreign type substance. PIC was made aware of this and cleaning/sanitizing of the baffle is taking place during the time of inspection. Ensure this baffle is regularly cleaned and sanitized to prevent growth of foreign substances and to maintain the integrity of the safety of the ice.
4-602.11: (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The meat and chili on the hot holding prep table registered at temperatures below the required 135 degrees F for hot holding. The meat, when probed, registered at 100 degrees F and had been in place since 10am this day. This container was disposed of and replaced with a fresh container of meat. The chili, when probed, registered at 123 degrees F and was in place at 1pm. Using time instead of temperature, the facility must dispose of the chili in the container at 5pm to ensure its food safety integrity. If this steam table is to have continued use, then the establishment must maintain a time control log where the food is replaced every 4 hours or the steam table needs to be turned up in temperature or maintenance needs to be requested for the equipment to be fixed or replaced. The facility is going to be using a controlled substance, more than likely a pan of water, to test the temperature availability of the steam table and to better gauge if they need it fixed, replaced, or simply turned up in temperature.
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: The ice scoop at the drive thru was observed to be stored with the scoop inside the ice machine where the handle was in contact with the ice. The scoop was removed and education was given to the drive thru worker at the time that this practice is unacceptable. Ensure that staff is trained on all proper storage methods that prevents contamination of food items and that the ice scoop is stored properly.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The caulking by the double sink in the back and by the grill on the prep table appears to be soiled and degrading. Ensure this caulking is removed from these locations and is replaced with fresh caulk in a manner that makes a good seal with the wall and allows the material to be smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed chili and cheese sauce being hot held below 135F. Chili measured tobe 130F(probed). Cheese sauce measured to be 118F. Employee stated new water was added to steam table. Ensure all hot held food is maintained at 135F or above. Corrected. Both products have been rapidly reheated to 165F. Products were out for 1 hour or less.  Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed eggs to be 55F in cold holding unit. Ensure all cold-held food is maintained at 41F or below. Corrected. Practice will cease. Eggs discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed black residue on ice machine. Ensure all non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as needed to prevent build-up. Clean ice machine.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: Facility is not able to provide proof of certified food protection manager certification for any employee at the time of the inspection. Each certified food protection manager must have proof of successful completion of an ANSI approved course available at the time of inspection.
findings.citation_text: 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the heat lamp with dripping grease and food debris, 2) the ice scoop holder where the ice scoop is stored at the drive thru window with water and what appears to be mold, 3) the milk spout on the bulk milk dispenser at the shake station with what appears to be mold, 4) the slicer with food debris, 5) the magnetic knife strip at the prep station with debris, 6) the ice flap in the ice machine with what appears to be mold/slime. Employees were instructed to begin working on cleaning and sanitizing these areas during the inspection to correct the violation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed sliced tomatoes in a shallow pan in the prep cooler to be probed at an internal temperature of 47F. Tomatoes were reported to have been stocked approximately 2 hours ago. They were transferred to a deeper pan and will be discarded at 4 pm (time control for 6 hours between 41-70F). Salsa that was in a deeper pan was probed at 42F so it appears as though the depth of the pan is the issue.

Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly chilled to less than 41°F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.comment: Observed coffee filters sitting on the counter unprotected in the waitress station.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11  (C) Single-service articles are not protected from contamination. Single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food and lip contact surfaces are protected from contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Active managerial control is lacking in the facility today. PIC was unable to designate employees to handle other tasks so that he could address Foodborne Illness Risk Factors identified during the inspection, and was unable to correctly instruct dish person on how to prepare and utilize the three compartment sink for manual wash, rinse sanitize process. PIC stated to wash, rinse and air dry. 
2-102.11(A) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate knowledge of of numerous sections of the food code . Discussed related sections of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(A).
findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(B) (Pf) PIC is not a certified food manager. Provide proof of Food Service Sanitation Manager Certification.  Reference 2-102.11(B).

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment: No certified food protection manager is present at the time of the inspection. PIC showed inspector the half paper from renewing his FSSMC in 2009 but had no other proof of CFPM. Provide proof of successful completion of a valid CFPM course for the PIC during each shift. 750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed a server wash hands, use bare hands to turn off the faucet, dry hands and then scratch face with clean hands. Other employees on the cook and make lines were observed to be doing other tasks, enter the cook/make line area and immediately put on gloves and handle food without proper hand washing first. Hand washing and glove use was discussed with the PIC. 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment: Observed the employee in the shake station taking the tickets out of the printer and with bare hands placing the paper ticket down in the whip cream on the top of the shakes. Employee was addressed and this practice was discussed--avoid placing tickets in shakes, especially since they are handled with bare hands that are doing multiple tasks without proper hand washing. 3-301.11 (Pf) Food employee is not minimizing bare hand contact with foods that are not in a ready to eat form. Employee shall use suitable utensils or gloves to minimize bare hand contact with these foods. Reference 3-301.11.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Observed raw sausage stored above packets of ready to eat sauces on the speed rack in the walk in cooler. Store ready to eat foods above raw foods. 3-302.11  (P)   Store ready to eat foods  above raw foods so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 1) Multiple sanitizer buckets tested at 0-100 ppm quaternary ammonium solution. The wall unit dispenser was also testing at 0-100 ppm quaternary ammonium. PIC was unable to step away and call EcoLab because he was on the make line. Sanitizer buckets need to be re-made and prepared manually if dispenser is not working appropriately, but PIC does not exhibit that this is possible as no liquid sanitizer is able to be located during the inspection. 2) Observed the dish machine, which was in use, to be testing at 0-10 ppm on the first time it was tested. Subsequent runs provided 25 ppm according to their EcoLab test strip, and inspector's maximum registering thermometer read 140F for the rinse cycle. pH of the water is unknown. EcoLab chlorine sanitizer states to dispense at 50-100 ppm, and it is not at this time.  3) The slicer at the back prep table is soiled with what appears to be food debris and mold. Wash, rinse and sanitize the slicer. Inspector spoke with Nick from EcoLab on the phone and explained the situation and he will be here to correct the sanitizer concentrations. 4-501.114  (P)  A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution. Options: 25ppm to 49ppm when the temperature is at least 120°F and the pH is 10 or less; or (2) 50ppm to 99ppm when the temperature is at least 100°F and the pH is 10 or less, or when the temperature is at least 75°F and the pH is 8 or less; or (3) 100ppm when the temperature is at least 55°F and the pH is 10 or less. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Cooked chicken tenders hot holding on top of the heat lamp were probed at 130-131F. Hot time and temperature control for safety foods must be hot held at 135F or above. This was discussed and chicken will be discarded. 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P)  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge.  Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Shell eggs in a pan in the cold holding insert area next to the grill were probed at 50F. Eggs were discarded during the inspection. Cold TCS foods must be held at 41F or below. 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment: There are numerous chemical spray bottles in EcoLab bottles in the mop sink area that do not have any sort of labeling on them. All chemicals must be labeled with the common name of the contents. 7-102.11  (Pf) Containers of toxic materials must be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed single portion cups of chili in the top of the pan in the prep cooler that were probed at 80F. Employee states she just portioned these before inspector arrived, and stocked them in the cooler. There is a pan of the same in the cooler underneath the prep cooler. Older, cold portioned chili was observed in the bottom of the pan in the top of the prep cooler. Hot chili cups were removed and placed in the walk in cooler to cool. Use adequate refrigeration that will cool TCS foods rapidly. Cooling method for single portion chili is inadequate. 3-501.15  (Pf) Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: No thermometer is observed in the milk dispenser in the wait station and the outside thermometer reads that it is in the temperature danger zone when the milk within is 33F. Provide an accurate and conspicuously placed thermometer in each cooling unit. 4-204-112  (C) Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Observed numerous fruit/drain flies throughout the facility. Most notably, flies are observed in the dish room, in the shake area and near that adjacent hand washing sink, and in the waitress area. Provide effective pest control. 6-501.111  (Pf) The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate fruit/drain flies, using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: Observed a pile of wet wiping cloths stored within the front hand washing sink at the beginning of the inspection. Cloths were removed. Store sanitizer cloths in the appropriate area. 3-304.14  (C) Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: 1) Observed the handle to the fry scoop to be stored in contact with the fries. 2) Observed the handle to one of the sauces in the prep cooler to be stored with the handle almost completely submerged in the food itself. Store in use utensils with the handle extended up and out of the foods. 3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: There are a couple of sleeves of cups and a couple of boxes of single service items on the floor in the dry storage area in the office, and coffee filters stored unprotected in the wait station. . Store single service items at least 6" off of the floor and covered and protected from contamination. 4-903.11(A) and (C)  (C) Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A) and (C).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Boards that are used to hold burgers and sandwiches as they are moved from the grill to the dressing station have edges that are rough with multiple different layers of the material exposed on both the ends and in the middle of some of the boards where they have seemed to have chipped. Food contact surfaces must be smooth, nonabsorbent, easily cleanable and free from unnecessary ledges or cracks. Replace boards. 4-202.11  (Pf) A food-contact surface that is not smooth and easily cleanable can harbor bacteria that con be transfer to food. Replace with a National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI approved surface. Reference 4-202.11.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: When dish machine was not testing correctly, three compartment sink was uncovered to be used and sinks were observed soiled with mold, moldy foods and other debris. Sinks were scrubbed during the inspection. 4-501.14  (C) Manual warewashing three compartment sink is soiled with food debris. The three compartment sink should be cleaned before use, as needed throughout the day, or at least once every 24 hours to ensure proper sanitizing of equipment and utensils. Clean the 3 compartment sink in the frequency listed previously. Reference 4-501.14.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the heat lamp for the fries with grease accumulation, 2) the weights on the wrappers with food debris, 3) the inside of the shake reach in freezer with food spillage, 4) the handles to the shake reach in freezers are sticky, 5) the top and sides of the dish machine with limescale accumulation, 6) the undersides of the tables in the dish room with debris (this is not helping the fly issue) and 7) most of the reach in freezers have significant soiled ice accumulation within. Clean these non-food contact surfaces. 4-602.13  (C) Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Walls and floors throughout the facility were observed soiled as well as the floor drain underneath the dish machine. Walls in the dish room need a thorough scrubbing as well as floor to wall junctions throughout the facility. Clean walls, floors and floor drains. 6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed milk in the dispenser in the wait station to not be date marked with the date of opening. The dispensing tube that is outside of the machine appears to be cut closer to a 180 degree angle as opposed to the 45 degree angle it is supposed to be cut at. Make sure tube is cut at an angle and that milk is date marked with the date of opening and held no longer than 7 days maximum. Coleslaw in the walk in cooler was not date marked either, however, manager stated that this was made this morning.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
1) Observed a cell phone sitting in a food prep area with active food prep occurring. Do not store cell phones in food prep areas. Not only can cell phones contaminate surfaces, the urge to reach for them and touch them while prepping food is there as well. 2) Observed raw sausage patties stored above hot dogs in the walk in cooler. Store all raw foods above ready to eat foods in refrigeration. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
No sanitizer was testing in the dish machine at the time of the inspection. A call was placed to EcoLab and Randy stated he would be at the facility within 45 minutes to correct the issue. Dish washing will cease until Randy can fix the machine.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment:
Observed a sanitizer bucket at the front grill and one at the drive thru area to test at 0-10 ppm quaternary ammonium solution. Buckets were taken to be re-made at the time of the inspection. Make sure all sanitizer buckets test at 200-400 ppm quaternary ammonium, which may mean they need to be changed at shorter intervals.
750-810b Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) the top of the dish machine with limescale accumulation, 2) the fry warmer and adjacent areas with significant grease accumulation, 3) the front hand washing sink with soil (it appears as though this sink is being used as a dump sink and not just as a hand washing sink), 4) the outside of a container of ice cream toppings in the walk in cooler soiled with what appears to be mold.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the wall in the walk in cooler to be soiled with what appears to be mold. Clean the wall.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed coleslaw and salsa in the walk in cooler that were not date marked with the date of preparation or date of opening. Coleslaw is reported to be made every other day and salsa is made daily. Date mark all ready to eat foods with the date of preparation or opening and hold no longer than 7 days maximum.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment:
Observed gravy cooling in the walk in cooler that was not marked with the time the cooling process began. Manager states they began cooling gravy at 10:30 am and gravy was probed at 57-64F four hours later. It is unknown whether it reached 70F within 2 hours as this is not tracked anywhere. Gravy was discarded. Gravy must be marked with the time the cooling process begins and cooled to 70F within 2 hours and then to 41F or below within an additional 4 hours. 
750-140(b)  Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - (x2) A) (R) Creamer packets were 53F-67F at the soda counter. Creamer packets were discarded in the trash. Ice had melted in the storage unit used for packets. Manager replaced ice and placed new packets in the container. B) Hotdogs, cheese slices, shell eggs, and liquid eggs at small cold holding unit between the grill and steam table were 48F-79F. Foods were discarded and new product placed in a cooler on the cook line. Cold potentially hazardous foods must be maintained at 41F/below. Maintain cold potentially hazardous foods at proper temperature. (see general comments)

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - A) Foods in freezers (ice cream, hash rounds) and on steam table (gravy) were uncovered. Keep foods covered between uses to protect foods from potential contamination. B) Ice bins were observed open during periods of time when drinks were not being made. Close lids to ice bins during slow periods/when drinks are not being made to protect ice from potential contamination. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.citation_text: 750.290 - Ice scoops were observed inside the ice bins between uses with handles in contact with the ice. Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice. Properly store ice scoops.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) can opener blade (dried food debris); B) plastic container holding miscellaneous utensils/equipment (crumbs/debris); & C) top inside microwaves (food splash). Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) walkin cooler shelves; B) area below grills (grease/food); C) general surfaces of cook line equipment and inside fryer panels (grease/food debris); D) bottom inside freezer & coolers; E) (R) fat boy caddy (heavy grease buildup); F) (R) outside/general surfaces of bulk milk dispenser; G) dust pans (buildup); & H) cracker/jam packet storage containers under order window. Clean the above items and all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.citation_text: 750.880 - A) Plastic utensil storage container at drive thru was soiled, and knives were observed facing different directions (food surfaces/handles intermixed). B) Coffee filters were observed uncovered at the drink counter. C) Portion cup/lid containers on cook line had debris in them. Maintain storage containers clean, store utensils all facing with handles extended out, and store single service items covered/inverted to protect items from potential contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - Sprayer sink basin has loose seal on the underside and mold buildup was present. Leaks appeared to be present at one handle of the faucet and possibly at the attached plumbing under the sink. Have a licensed plumber repair the sink in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.citation_text: 750.1120 - (R) Handsinks are clearly being used for purposes other than handwashing. Back handsink had food debris and a soiled paper towel in the basin, while handsink across from sundae prep had food debris buildup down in the drain. Handsinks are to be accessible for handwashing at all times and are to be used only for handwashing. Use handsinks properly and maintain them clean. Proper use of handsinks was once again discussed with management.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - (x2) A) Whipped topping in top portion of sundae prep cooler was 62F (topping was checked with stem thermometer in a cup). The bottle of whipped topping was discarded in the trash by the manager. B) Creamer packets were at 67F at the soda counter. Creamer packets were discarded in the trash. Ice had melted in the storage unit used for packets. Manager replaced ice and placed new packets in the container. Cold potentially hazardous foods must be maintained at 41F/below. Maintain cold potentially hazardous foods at proper temperature.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Vegetable soup in hot holding well across from soda machine was at 125F. Soup was discarded during the inspection. Manager had to add water to the hot holding well and then placed a new batch of soup in the unit. New batch of soup was at 142F. Hot potentially hazardous foods must be maintained at 135F/above. Maintain hot potentially hazardous foods at proper temperature. **Keep plenty of water in steam units to ensure proper temperatures are maintained**

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Front section on the top of the sundae prep cooler (across from drive thru) used for storing whipped topping was at 60F. Refrigeration units used for storage of potentially hazardous foods must be able to maintain products at 41F/below. Discontinue use of the front section on the top of the sundae prep cooler until it can maintain potentially hazardous products at 41F/below. (see general comments)

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Blue ice scoop holder had buildup of mold and other debris in the bottom. Ice scoop holder and ice scoops were taken to the dish area to be cleaned/sanitized. All foods and clean utensils/equipment must be protected from cross contamination at all times. Clean the ice scoops and holder daily/as needed.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750.120a - Containers of blueberries and strawberries in the walkin freezer were uncovered. Also some containers were stacked so the bottom of the containers were in direct contact with the food in the container below. Food shall be protected at all times. Keep foods covered between use and provide a barrier between the bottoms of containers and the foods in the containers below to prevent potential cross contamination.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.290 - Large metal container with no handle on top of ice machine has been used for dispensing ice according to manager. Ice shall be dispensed only with scoops, tongs, or other ice dispensing utensils.  Provide appropriate utensils for dispensing food (must have handle, no bowls used)

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment: 750280 & 290 - A) Knife on cook line was observed in sanitizer solution. Cook and manager were advised as to proper utensil storage and use of 4 hour rule. Knife and container of solution were taken to the dish area to be cleaned/sanitized. Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food, clean and dry, in running potable water dipper wells. B) Ice scoops were observed in soiled container (see #7b). Ice scoops and container were taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized. Ice scoops shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text: 750.160 & 510 - Cook was observed using wet wiping cloth and then returned to food prep without washing his hands/putting on a new pair of gloves. Cook washed his hands and put on a new pair of gloves after instructed to do so by the inspector. Gloves shall be single use and used for only one task.  Gloves must be discarded when damaged, soiled or after an interruption in operations. Hands must also be washed before putting on gloves, between glove changes and as needed when hands become contaminated. **Management needs to have a refresher on proper handwashing/glove use with staff**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750.650a - A) Lid of onion storage bin in walkin cooler is cracked. B) Ice scoops are worn, and one has a chunk broken off at the end where the scoop comes in direct contact with the ice. Replace the onion storage bin and damaged ice scoops. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean

Properly clean and sanitize the above items and all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of food, mold, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

Clean the above items and all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - Back door had gaps at the bottom and along the side where light was visible. Outer openings shall be protected against the entrance of pests. Repair the back door so it is tight fitting and vermin proof.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean

Clean the walls in the walkin cooler and throughout daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text: 750.1300 - Multiple bottles containing pink and blue chemicals were not labeled as to the contents. Pink liquid was quat sanitizer (verified with test strip) & blue liquid was glass cleaner. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label spray bottles as to their contents. **Just because chemicals are a particular color does not mean labeling is not required** Spray bottles were labeled during the inspection.

findings.citation_text: 750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

750-530a Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.
